licenses.electedTerms: Modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik Vlaanderen
licenses.electedBecause: The grant is named in the dataset record and its articles sit in a separate instrument, and the two are reached from the service rather than from a search. `https://geo.api.vlaanderen.be/ad/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities`, 131,001 bytes, sha256 `317c2e322dde870fe7c2c6d2f9dec05e486bac96ae1ccd398638f090110d028b`, states `<Fees>Het gebruik van de service is kosteloos.</Fees>`, which prices the service rather than licensing the data, and points `AccessConstraints` at a `gebruiksrecht` page whose own words send the reader onward: `Gelieve de toegangs- en gebruiksbepalingen te raadplegen in de metadata van alle datasets die in de service worden aangeboden`. Its per-type `MetadataURL` gives CSW record `5c52b299-8f05-4d35-9839-a42934f1e619`, retrieved at `https://metadata.vlaanderen.be/srv/dut/csw?request=GetRecordById&service=CSW&version=2.0.2&ElementSetName=full&id=5c52b299-8f05-4d35-9839-a42934f1e619&OUTPUTSCHEMA=http://www.isotc211.org/2005/gmd`, 57,258 bytes, sha256 `71c827ecab5e485be1900b975849417ab3f47242e96fc97608f9493ef3d861b2`, whose title reads `Adressen`. That record carries two `MD_LegalConstraints` blocks and the distinction matters. The access block states `Geen beperkingen op de publieke toegang.` against the INSPIRE codelist term `noLimitations`. The re-use block names four instruments: `Modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik` at `https://data.vlaanderen.be/id/licentie/modellicentie-gratis-hergebruik/v1.0`, two instruments for public-task use by GDI-Vlaanderen participants and by bodies that are not participants, and the attribution string `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`. A re-user who is neither a participant nor a public body acting on a public task holds the first, and the two GDI instruments govern a use this repository does not make. The articles are at `https://www.vlaanderen.be/digitaal-vlaanderen/onze-oplossingen/open-data/voorwaarden-voor-het-hergebruik-van-overheidsinformatie/modellicentie-gratis-hergebruik`, 71,446 bytes, sha256 `c195c42c0b8578d784e779a012137bfdc4e44cb55f7fee0dd2b13a3db04d1f2b`. The identifier itself serves no text: it answers `text/html`, `text/turtle`, `application/ld+json` and `application/rdf+xml` with one 541,080-byte application rendering to its title, and `.ttl` appended to the same path serves the RDF, which states `cc:requires cc:Attribution` and `dct:type adms:licencetype/Attribution`. Article 3 grants a non-exclusive, worldwide right to re-use the product for any lawful purpose, `met inbegrip van het reproduceren, doorgeven, publiceren, aanpassen en commercieel exploiteren`. Article 4 makes attribution the only use condition and lets the licensor specify its form, which this licensor has: `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`. Article 6 states that access, provision and re-use are free. Article 7 gives the licence indefinite duration. The instrument states its own compatibility with the Open Government Licence, the Licence Ouverte, CC BY 3.0 and ODC-By 1.0, and it carries no share-alike term. No SPDX identifier exists for it, so `spdx` is left out rather than approximating one, because `electedLicenseLabel` feeds the share-alike prefix filter.

fetch.because: Article 3 grants the right to reproduce and transmit the product, which is what paging the service performs, and article 6 states that access and provision are free.

extract.because: Article 3 grants adaptation (`aanpassen`) alongside reproduction, which covers reading the designator and the component references out of a feature. Article 2 defines intellectual property rights to include database rights, and article 3 grants re-use over the product rather than over a subset of those rights.

transform.because: Article 3 grants re-use for any lawful purpose including adaptation and commercial exploitation, so joining the four feature types into a token and tag corpus is granted. Article 4 adds one obligation that carries into the result: attribution as `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`.

train.because: Article 3 grants re-use for `elk rechtmatig doeleinde`, which covers reproducing the rows into a training process and adapting them. Article 5 states that the licensee holds the intellectual property in the works it creates on the basis of the product, which addresses the resulting weights directly. Article 4 requires that the re-use comply with data-protection law, which this source's `personalDataReview` addresses.

redistribute-data.because: Article 3 grants publication and transmission. Article 4 conditions it on the attribution the licensor specified, `Bron: Digitaal Vlaanderen`, and provides the wording for a combined work where listing every source is impractical: `bevat overheidsinformatie, verkregen onder de modellicentie voor gratis hergebruik Vlaanderen v1.0`. Article 4 also forbids suggesting that the re-use carries the licensor's endorsement.

redistribute-model.because: This instrument answers the question CC BY leaves open. Article 5 states that the licensee retains all intellectual property rights in the works it creates on the basis of the product, `zonder evenwel afbreuk te doen aan de verplichtingen betreffende het hergebruik van het product in deze werken`. Trained weights are such a work, so they are the licensee's, and the product's attribution obligation carries into them.

commercial-sublicense.because: Article 3 grants a non-exclusive right to the licensee and states no sublicensing right, and article 5 reserves to the licensor every right the licence does not grant. Unlike CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(5)(A), this instrument makes no direct offer to a downstream recipient, so whether a recipient holds it by taking the product under the same standing public licence is a question the text does not answer. Article 7 also ends the licence of right on breach, which a sublicence would have to account for.

The service feed at `https://geoservices.wallonie.be/inspire/atom/AD_Service.xml`, 9,935 bytes, sha256 `46c3db24852e6f68`, adds `Accès libre et gratuit au service pour tout public` and the INSPIRE codelist term `noLimitations`, which are access statements rather than the use grant. fetch.because: CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(A) grants the right to reproduce and share the Licensed Material in whole, which is what retrieving the zipped GML performs, and the feed states free access to the service.

extract.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing and reproducing Adapted Material, and the publisher's own gloss states that the user may use and modify the data to derive a work.

transform.because: The same clause grants adaptation for any purpose, commercial purposes included, with §3(a)(1)(B) requiring that modifications be indicated. The publisher's gloss names derivation of a work explicitly.

train.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants reproduction and §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material. Fitting a model performs both: it reproduces the material into the training process and produces an adaptation of it. CC BY 4.0 attaches no share-alike condition, so the grant does not reach the resulting weights.

redistribute-data.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants sharing in any medium, conditioned by §3(a) on crediting the licensor. The SPW has specified the credit to use, which is the `Source : Service public de Wallonie (SPW) …` string its record carries.

redistribute-model.because: Whether trained weights are Adapted Material under CC BY 4.0 is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records. commercial-sublicense.because: CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(5)(A) offers every downstream recipient a licence from the Licensor directly and grants no sublicensing right. Whether that satisfies a commercial agreement is a drafting question this text does not answer.

licenses.electedTerms: Nutzungsbedingungen für kostenlose Geodaten und Geodienste (OGD) von swisstopo
licenses.electedBecause: swisstopo links its own terms from the dataset, which is how they were found rather than guessed: four candidate terms URLs answered HTTP 404, and the STAC collection at `https://data.geo.admin.ch/api/stac/v1/collections/ch.swisstopo.amtliches-gebaeudeadressverzeichnis` carries a link with `rel: license` pointing at `https://www.swisstopo.admin.ch/ogd-conditions`, titled `Terms of use`, alongside `providers` naming `Federal Office of Topography - swisstopo` with the roles `producer` and `licensor`. The collection's own `license` field reads `proprietary`, which is swisstopo's marker for its own conditions rather than an instrument; reading that field as the licence would record this publication as closed. The conditions, 261,514 bytes, sha256 `1f717c01937fff78`, published 26 August 2022, state in clause 2 that `The free geodata and geoservices of swisstopo may be used, distributed and made accessible. Furthermore, they may be enriched and processed and also used commercially. A reference to the source is mandatory.`, and they specify the source reference to attach, of which the English form is `Federal Office of Topography swisstopo` and the short form `©swisstopo`. Clause 1 grounds this in the Federal Act on Geoinformation and its ordinance. Clause 3 is the one condition worth carrying forward: `In the event of excessive use of the geoservices infrastructure, access may be restricted or refused`, and swisstopo may then conclude a contract with the user. That clause governs the geoservices infrastructure, and this row records a file download rather than a service. The publisher's own page for the directory states that it is published `for use free of charge by everyone` and `can be used by the public administration, as well as by companies for commercial purposes`. **This election grants the terms and does not make the source ingest-eligible**: its `personalDataReview` reads `present`, which `ingestEligibilityProblems` refuses on its own.

fetch.because: Clause 2 grants use, distribution and making accessible, and the publisher's page states the directory is free of charge for everyone. The download is a file rather than a geoservice, so clause 3's excessive-use condition does not reach it.

extract.because: Clause 2 grants that the data `may be enriched and processed`, which covers reading the street label, house number and postcode out of a row.

transform.because: The same clause grants processing and commercial use, subject to the mandatory source reference.

train.because: Clause 2 grants use, reproduction and commercial exploitation of the data, which is what fitting a model on the rows performs. The source reference is owed on any resulting publication.

redistribute-data.because: Clause 2 grants distribution and making accessible, conditioned on attaching one of the specified source references, which for English is `Federal Office of Topography swisstopo`.

redistribute-model.because: Whether trained weights are a representation or publication requiring the source reference, and whether they are a derivative at all, is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records. Clause 2 names digital representations, publications and dissemination, which does not settle weights.

commercial-sublicense.because: The conditions grant use to the user and state no sublicensing right, and clause 3 contemplates a contract for heavy use, so whether a downstream recipient holds these terms directly is a question the text does not answer.

extract.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material, which covers reading the number, street, postcode and municipality columns out of a row.

train.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants reproduction and §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material, commercial purposes included, and CC BY 4.0 carries no share-alike term.

licenses.refusedBecause: HM Land Registry licenses Price Paid Data in two parts, and the part this repository reads is the restricted one. The download page, `https://www.gov.uk/government/statistical-data-sets/price-paid-data-downloads`, 129,747 bytes, sha256 `1f3aab231a5a27359dd7ef94c39970eed918395626e7b9f267fafca2282f89f3`, states `Price Paid Data is released under the Open Government Licence (OGL)` with the attribution `Contains HM Land Registry data © Crown copyright and database right 2021. This data is licensed under the Open Government Licence v3.0.`, and then: `However, OGL does not cover the use of third party rights, which we are not authorised to license. Price Paid Data contains address data processed against Ordnance Survey’s AddressBase Premium product, which incorporates Royal Mail’s PAF® database (Address Data). Royal Mail and Ordnance Survey permit your use of Address Data in the Price Paid Data: for personal and/or non-commercial use; to display for the purpose of providing residential property price information services. If you want to use the Address Data in any other way, you must contact Royal Mail.` The same page defines the Address Data as `Postcode`, `PAON`, `SAON`, `Street`, `Locality`, `Town/City`, `District` and `County`. Those eight fields are every field this repository takes from the file: the house number, street, locality, county and postcode of a Great Britain address skeleton. OGL v3.0 itself, `https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/`, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`, excludes `third party rights the Information Provider is not authorised to license`. Training a general-purpose address parser, publishing rows that carry these fields, and shipping an index built from them are neither personal nor non-commercial use, and none of them displays residential property prices, so the OGL grant reaches the price, date and property-type columns and not the address. The route to permission is Royal Mail, at the `address.management@royalmail.com` address the page names. The guidance page `https://www.gov.uk/guidance/about-the-price-paid-data`, 130,925 bytes, sha256 `1ec6dda91071cf30490b6077e212bfc6938c330645d391a59c2ec24a54d6e704`, states that `Addresses used by HM Land Registry to describe land are mostly derived from Royal Mail address data`, which agrees. This is the reading MHCLG's energy performance notice gave for `gb-property-building-2`, from a second publisher whose address fields pass through the same AddressBase Premium match.

The Valuation Office Agency publishes the non-domestic rating lists under its own restricted terms and states that the Open Government Licence does not apply. Its download page, `https://voaratinglists.blob.core.windows.net/html/rlidata.htm`, 33,414 bytes, sha256 `dafa09c510cf68e3575adbdd256a7b95ff86f1193ecaeda5dce6bd355df49be0`, reads `VO Rating List Downloads are only available under our restricted` license terms and `open government licence does not apply`, and `The information must be used in line with the restricted license terms and conditions`. The row's note describes the lists as the commercial complement to Price Paid Data, which makes this the largest Great Britain business-premises register refused so far. The route to permission is the VOA's restricted license, whose clauses this reading did not open.

licenses.electedTerms: Open Government Licence v3.0
licenses.electedBecause: Ordnance Survey licenses four OS OpenData products, Code-Point Open, OS Open Names, OS Open Roads and OS Open USRN, under the Open Government Licence v3.0. Each download ships a `licence.txt`, and each one states `Your use of OS OpenData is subject to the terms at http://os.uk/opendata/licence` (Code-Point Open words it `Your use of data is subject to terms at www.ordnancesurvey.co.uk/opendata/licence`). Both addresses redirected on 2026-10-14 to `https://www.nationalarchives.gov.uk/doc/open-government-licence/version/3/`, 10,450 bytes, sha256 `f5b2b9f2af63647cde889fa6c3508f5705925295b74912c68caa28dd37e64aa5`. OS's own `docs.os.uk` terms page, 2,936 bytes, sha256 `83e7e1047ff833d4144e451f596290543b5673915733d3a26b8d48cac5253d7e`, states that the OS OpenData terms `are contained within the Open Government Licence` and that the attribution statement `can be found in the licence file downloaded with the data`. The licence files read are Code-Point Open 2026-08, 346 bytes, sha256 `2273fa3818d2b009ab38c11f3cfc9563e48c0e9e940bf73c1a3685b3188255ad`; OS Open Names 2026-07, 438 bytes, sha256 `1be838dcdba14daa10f6a5015833100858711fcda9e495a9442c9295d357f99f`; OS Open Roads 2026-04, 190 bytes, sha256 `65f3f555aa3e42e93b4db24a29ad277beefd12bc4871076d558c1cc41a6b216d`; and OS Open USRN 2026-10, 442 bytes, sha256 `41e89b74974c31cbb39efec9d78db825107e8fca565611e7098f92c94c6be62e`. The attribution differs by product. Open Roads requires `Contains Ordnance Survey data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Code-Point Open and Open Names add `Contains Royal Mail data © Royal Mail copyright and database right 2026` and `Contains National Statistics data © Crown copyright and database right 2026`. Open USRN requires `Contains OS data © Crown Copyright and database rights 2026` and, `Where you use data relating to Scotland`, `This product contains data created and maintained by Scottish Local Government.` No licence file or page read restricts the Royal Mail-derived postcode data beyond that acknowledgement, which is a statement about the text read; the OGL's own exemption for `third party rights the Information Provider is not authorised to license` stays in force. Code-Point Open's `product-supply` page, 4,936 bytes, sha256 `3f71e7910ce3a0107af8217563eb8e193a715c37e91bb5166078fae8ebeb942a`, states `Code-Point Open covers postcodes for Great Britain`, and the 2026-08 release has no BT area, so no Northern Ireland postcode and no Land & Property Services term reaches these sources. This reading covers the licence only. A row that joins a real street to a real postcode and synthesizes a house number can reproduce a residential address, which is a question for the personal-data review in `source-resolutions.json`, not for this reading.

What this body adds is the evidence that the grant reaches these ten territories, which the metropolitan file alone does not show. **The Base Adresse Nationale publishes one gzipped CSV per INSEE department code beside the national extract, at the same path and under the same dataset record.** `https://adresse.data.gouv.fr/data/ban/adresses/latest/csv/` lists 107 department files, among them the three-digit codes 971, 972, 973, 974, 975, 976, 977, 978, 984, 986, 987, 988 and 989. Electing here does not disturb that refusal.

fetch.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants the right to reproduce, copy and publish the Information freely and for any purpose, which is what downloading one department's gzipped CSV performs.

extract.because: The same grant covers extracting and transforming the Information, which is reading `numero`, `nom_voie`, `code_postal` and `nom_commune` out of a row.

transform.because: The licence permits adapting, modifying and combining the Information with other information, which is what normalising a row into this repository's components does.

train.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 names no restriction on the purpose of reuse and attaches no share-alike term, so training a model on the Information falls inside `librement, pour tout usage`. licenses.electedBecause: The publisher states one licence on the dataset itself. `https://data.public.lu/api/1/datasets/adresses-georeferencees-bd-adresses/`, 15,628 bytes, sha256 `d8bd134083437b075433459deb908b823a7a7fcf1a7470b0502032aed10620bd`, answers `title` `Adresses géoréférencées (BD-Adresses)`, `organization` `Administration du cadastre et de la topographie`, `license` `cc-zero`, `frequency` `weekly` and `last_modified` `2026-09-28T02:31:48.330000+00:00`, with five resources of which three are bulk files: `addresses.csv` at 28,186,970 bytes, `addresses.geojson` at 80,836,067 and `addresses-shp.zip` at 19,681,289. `cc-zero` is data.public.lu's identifier for the CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication, whose only version is 1.0, so `spdx` reads `CC0-1.0`. One statement of the publisher's is carried into `coverage` rather than smoothed over: it describes BD-Adresses as `un sous-ensemble des adresses figurant dans le registre national des localités et des rues`, a subset of the national register enriched with coordinates, georeferenced on the cadastral parcel and the digitised cadastral plan.

fetch.because: CC0 §3 waives every copyright and related right the Affirmer holds, to the greatest extent permitted by law, so downloading the published CSV is unreserved.

extract.because: The same waiver covers extraction and database rights, which §2 names among the rights waived, so reading the street, number, locality and postcode columns is unreserved.

transform.because: §2 waives the rights to reproduce, adapt, distribute and perform, in every medium and for any purpose, so producing a token and tag corpus from the rows is unreserved.

train.because: CC0 reserves no act at all, so fitting a model on the rows is unreserved.

redistribute-data.because: §2 waives the distribution right without condition. Crediting the ACT stays good practice and CC0 requires it nowhere.

redistribute-model.because: The question that stands open under CC BY and ODbL, whether trained weights are a derivative of the rows, does not arise here: CC0 waives the rights that would make the answer matter, and §3 adds a fallback licence to exercise all those rights unconditionally where the waiver is ineffective in law.

commercial-sublicense.because: §3's fallback grant is royalty-free, non-transferable, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, irrevocable and unconditional, and it runs to the public rather than to one recipient, so a downstream party holds it directly. The waiver in §2 leaves no right that would need sublicensing.

licenses.electedBecause: The Ministry states one condition of use and states it twice, in its own register and in that register's INSPIRE export. Reaching it took reading an error body rather than another search: the export URL the service's own capabilities document writes answers HTTP 422 with `{"loc":["path","collection_record_id"],"msg":"value is not a valid uuid"}`, which places the id in the PATH where the capabilities put it in the query, and a second 422 enumerates the permitted `export_format` values, among which `gmd` does not appear. `https://rpi.gov.sk/api/collection_record/86dea70e-a55b-4241-bd63-4024b3f76b72`, 9,335 bytes, sha256 `0937d4bffc3f3078e27aad12dc3649469969ec407a022da81125f2656ff6ff38`, is the record: `title` `INSPIRE - Adresy`, `unit_name` `Ministerstvo vnútra Slovenskej republiky`, `hierarchy_level` `dataset`, `status` `published`, `date_stamp` `2025-05-28`. It ties to the measured service by its own `downloadable_urls`, which holds exactly `https://rageo.minv.sk/geoserver/ad/wfs?service=WFS&version=2.0.0&request=GetCapabilities`, and its `spatial_scopes` reads the INSPIRE codelist term `national` with a `footprint_geo` of `Slovenská Republika` at a 100% match. Its `use_constraints` reads `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky (CC0 Voľné dielo)`. The same record exported as `export_format=inspire_xml`, 18,955 bytes, sha256 `710e0fc3216645b5c4014a4044dbaff86adc07da390b8a06b0e99055decdf28e`, carries `accessConstraints` and `useConstraints` both as `otherRestrictions`, the ISO code meaning that the statement is in `otherConstraints`, and two `otherConstraints` values: `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky (CC0 Voľné dielo)` and `Neuplatňujú sa žiadne podmienky`. That phrase renders INSPIRE's controlled value for no conditions applying to access and use, in Slovak, as ČÚZK's `žádné podmínky neplatí` does in Czech. The parenthetical adds the publisher's own identification of it as CC0. No version accompanies that label, so `spdx` and `termsVersion` are left out and `electedTerms` records the publisher's words, the same treatment Czechia's entry receives. The record also reads `is_opendata_allowed` and `is_hvd_compliant` true, so the Ministry publishes this as a high-value dataset under the Open Data Directive. The CC BY 4.0 an earlier pass recorded for Slovakia belongs to the geodesy authority's ATOM feed at `inspirews.skgeodesy.sk` and grants nothing over this service, which is a different publisher.

extract.because: A statement that no conditions apply reserves no act, so reading the designator and the component references out of a feature is unreserved. CC0, which the publisher names, waives extraction and database rights explicitly.

transform.because: No condition attaches to adaptation, so joining the five feature types into a token and tag corpus is unreserved.

train.because: No condition attaches to any purpose, so fitting a model on the rows is unreserved.

redistribute-data.because: A statement that no conditions apply imposes no attribution condition, and CC0 imposes none either. Crediting the Ministry stays good practice and neither statement requires it.

redistribute-model.because: The question that stands open under CC BY and ODbL, whether trained weights are a derivative of the rows, does not arise where the publisher states that no conditions apply and names CC0, which waives the rights that would make the answer matter.

commercial-sublicense.because: A statement that no conditions apply leaves no right that would need sublicensing. CC0 §3 adds a fallback licence to exercise all those rights unconditionally where the waiver is ineffective in law, and it runs to the public rather than to one recipient.

The NOS convention `https://interop.esante.gouv.fr/ig/nos/attach/NOS_ConventionNOS_V2.0.pdf` (1,168,464 bytes, sha256 `f6260123b6867264b763bfaaa7a180cab7d3db489af9a559e8fe6b32d73c253e`) reserves rights over itself, `Ce document est la propriété de l'ANS - Son utilisation, sa reproduction ou sa diffusion sans l'autorisation préalable et écrite de l'ANS sont interdites` ("This document is the property of the ANS; its use, reproduction or distribution without the ANS's prior written authorisation is prohibited"), a footer on the convention document rather than a term over the nomenclatures, and says of the NOS only `Les NOS sont disponibles sur le site de l'ANS ... visualisables sur le serveur https://mos.esante.gouv.fr/NOS/` ("The NOS are available on the ANS site ... viewable on the server"). The SMT conditions, `https://smt.esante.gouv.fr/cgu/` (95,036 bytes, sha256 `dbcb5c85c4e95b697e90721a09bc2d3cdd8c152c30e64af034b3e67bbd26ed2f`), govern the terminology server rather than the mos.esante.gouv.fr files, grant at §10 a `droit d'utilisation du SMT ... pour usage propre` ("right to use the SMT ... for one's own use"), defer to each terminology's own licence, and list `Les dispositions du code des relations entre le public et l'administration (CRPA)` in their applicable legal frame; the SMT catalogue renders its per-terminology licences in script and the retained copy shows none for TRE_R35. The only data.gouv.fr dataset matching the NOS is published by InterHop under `odc-odbl` (`datagouv-search-nos.json`, 5,386 bytes, sha256 `b37beab92add842df94ad1b5e86327c2200975822c4207201df0b7486a244d46`), a third party's licence on its own compilation and not the publisher's. ANS is a groupement d'intérêt public, a legal person of public law, so it is an administration under CRPA L. 300-2. The CRPA text retrieved from codes.droit.org (2,931,595 bytes, sha256 `88bd56805aff26399099f6acce38b055d2e2c63242c6bdfbbc85f115145159bb`) reads at L. 321-1 `Les informations publiques figurant dans des documents communiqués ou publiés par les administrations mentionnées au premier alinéa de l'article L. 300-2 peuvent être utilisées par toute personne qui le souhaite à d'autres fins que celles de la mission de service public pour les besoins de laquelle les documents ont été produits ou reçus` ("Public information in documents communicated or published by the administrations named in L. 300-2 may be used by any person who wishes, for purposes other than the public-service mission for which the documents were produced or received"), and at L. 322-1 `Sauf accord de l'administration, la réutilisation des informations publiques est soumise à la condition que ces dernières ne soient pas altérées, que leur sens ne soit pas dénaturé et que leurs sources et la date de leur dernière mise à jour soient mentionnées` ("Unless the administration agrees, reuse is subject to the information not being altered, its meaning not being distorted, and its source and the date of its last update being stated"). L. 321-2 c) excludes information on which third parties hold intellectual property rights; a list of French street-type words authored by ANS carries none that the retrieved documents name. Legifrance answered HTTP 403 to every article URL, so the consolidated text is the codes.droit.org copy.

fetch.because: CRPA L. 321-1 permits any person to use public information that an administration publishes, and ANS publishes the file at mos.esante.gouv.fr.

extract.because: Reading the street-type labels out of the value set is use of the public information under L. 321-1.

transform.because: L. 321-1 permits use for any purpose other than the original mission. L. 322-1 forbids altering the information or distorting its meaning, which tagging an unmodified label such as `Ancien chemin` as a street type does not do.

train.because: Training is use `à d'autres fins que celles de la mission de service public` under L. 321-1, subject to stating the source and the date of last update under L. 322-1.

redistribute-data.because: L. 321-1 sets no limit on publication, and L. 322-1 requires the redistributed rows to state `Agence du Numérique en Santé, TRE_R35_TypeVoie` and its last update, 2023-12-15.

redistribute-model.because: The statutory right covers any reuse, commercial or not, and L. 326-1 names commercial reuse as lawful when L. 322-1's conditions are met. The model card states the source and date.

commercial-sublicense.because: The reuse right runs from the statute to `toute personne`, so a commercial licensee of the result holds it directly. L. 323-2 allows restrictions only through a licence, and ANS has established none for TRE_R35.

The entire Derivative Database; or b. A file containing all of the alterations made to the Database or the method of making the alterations`), and 4.8 (`You may not sublicense the Database.`). 4.4(b) makes the extracted address rows a Derivative Database, which the published training extract satisfies under ODbL 1.0. 4.5(b) states that `Using this Database, a Derivative Database, or this Database as part of a Collective Database to create a Produced Work does not create a Derivative Database for purposes of Section 4.4`. The OSMF board-endorsed Produced Work guideline, `https://osmfoundation.org/wiki/Licence/Community_Guidelines/Produced_Work_-_Guideline`, 42,647 bytes, sha256 `99b7c6cd7d8b2e23df72a60de68c941853d27980af6e9ae41be885af1242a895`, reads: `If the published result of your project is intended for the extraction of the original data, then it is a database and not a Produced Work. Otherwise it is a Produced Work. However, if you publish a produced work, the underlying database has to be published as well (or alternations to the original database as is the case of derived databases), according to section 4.6 of ODbL.` A parser's weights are not intended for extracting the original data, so they are a Produced Work, and the published extract meets 4.6. The extracts are read through Geofabrik, whose download page, `https://download.geofabrik.de/`, 9,609 bytes, sha256 `4b017225876c1edf6954a66da43dfb8104a7e7ecc93ca83f3d22c69eef59b570`, states `Data processed by Geofabrik GmbH and created by OpenStreetMap Contributors | License: ODbL 1.0`. The Substantial guideline, 44,919 bytes, sha256 `9a70503b9b062628cc63ddea60389dea9df9e51b0498551bf3d2b00289cf593f`, is retained. What this repository reads: address and name tags from Geofabrik extracts (`osm`, and the 2026-10-02 extracts for BD, CN, ID, IN, NG, PK, RU and VN), CN rows of the coarse-placer sample, the rendered BD and PK registers, and venue and sub-venue names from the Geofabrik GB, FR, DE and ES extracts plus OSM lexicon entries in `spliced-sub-venue`.

fetch.because: ODbL 3.1 grants a licence to `Use the Database`, and the copyright page states `You are free to copy`. Geofabrik republishes the extracts under ODbL 1.0.

extract.because: ODbL 3.1 grants Use of the Database, which includes Extraction; 4.4(b) states that Extraction of a Substantial part into a new database makes a Derivative Database, which the licence permits on the share-alike condition.

transform.because: The copyright page states `You are free to ... adapt our data`, and ODbL governs the adapted rows as a Derivative Database under 4.4.

train.because: 3.1 grants Use, `explicitly include[s] commercial use, and do[es] not exclude any field of endeavour`. Training on a Derivative Database creates a Produced Work, which 4.5(b) takes outside share-alike, on the 4.3 notice and the 4.6 offer of the Derivative Database.

redistribute-data.because: 4.2 and 4.4 permit Publicly Conveying a Derivative Database only under ODbL 1.0 (or a 4.4(a) compatible licence), with a copy or URI of the licence and the notices kept intact. The training extract is published as `sister-software/mailwoman-osm-training-extract` under ODbL 1.0 with `© OpenStreetMap contributors`. Any other published split or index that contains OSM-derived rows must carry the same terms; it cannot be published under the repository's own licence.

redistribute-model.because: Weights are a Produced Work under the OSMF guideline, so 4.5(b) leaves them outside share-alike. Publicly Using them needs the 4.3 notice that Contents came from OpenStreetMap under ODbL, carried in the model card and rights files, and 4.6 needs the offer of the Derivative Database, met by the published training extract.

commercial-sublicense.because: ODbL 4.8 states `You may not sublicense the Database. Each time You communicate the Database, the whole or Substantial part of the Contents, or any Derivative Database to anyone else in any way, the Licensor offers to the recipient a license to the Database on the same terms and conditions as this License.` A commercial agreement over the weights covers the Produced Work; it cannot grant rights in the OSM data or the extract, which a recipient takes from the OpenStreetMap Foundation under ODbL.

GURS's ISO 19139 record for the Register naslovov, `728e9d6a-46d0-4242-b8ef-255317da2ff3`, 64,175 bytes, sha256 `26faa9afdf5ae3b07c8fad1f8695616ce8b8ea431a48a4c5583adef31aa28260`, reads in `otherConstraints`: `Splošni pogoji uporabe geodetskih podatkov: https://www.e-prostor.gov.si/dostopi/javni-dostop/?acitem=1821-1822` and `Podatki so dostopni pod Creative Commons - Attribution 4.0 International (CC BY 4.0) licenco. (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0)`, with public access `noLimitations`. The general terms that record names, 179,936 bytes, sha256 `3a3ff6dafb55a20a358a4ed5e63378265f48b300188523e3f163dab6ad279f2d`, state: `Podatki Geodetske uprave imajo status informacij javnega značaja in so na voljo pod pogoji mednarodne licence Creative Commons 4.0. (priznanje avtorstva). … V skladu s to licenco je dovoljeno vsakomur, da podatke iz evidenc Geodetske uprave, nekomercialno in komercialno, uporablja pod pogojem navedbe vira podatkov. Dovoljeno je tako deljenje kot predelovanje podatkov. Uporabnik podatkov se obvezuje, da bo pri vsaki objavi podatkov ali izdelkov zagotovil navedbo vira podatkov, ki obsega » Geodetska uprava Republike Slovenije, vrsta podatka in čas, na katerega se podatki nanašajo oziroma datum stanja zbirke podatkov «.` The national portal's entry `register-naslovov`, publisher `GEODETSKA UPRAVA REPUBLIKE SLOVENIJE`, 52,416 bytes, sha256 `4345311030489430b138da4e704a2c56bba3e26484036d18a5c2833b331d758f`, gives `licence` `Priznanje avtorstva (CC BY 4.0)` and lists the `Javni geodetski podatki (JGP)` application, which is the host OpenAddresses fetches from, among its resources.

fetch.because: CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(A) grants reproducing and sharing the Licensed Material, which is what downloading the JGP composite product performs.

extract.because: GURS's terms state `Dovoljeno je tako deljenje kot predelovanje podatkov`, that sharing and adapting are both allowed, which covers reading the street, house number, settlement and postcode fields.

transform.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants adaptation, which GURS's terms restate as `predelovanje`, and §3(a)(1)(B) requires modifications to be indicated when shared.

train.because: GURS's terms allow use `nekomercialno in komercialno`, on the condition of the source statement, and CC BY 4.0 carries no share-alike term.

redistribute-data.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants sharing. GURS requires every publication of data or products to carry `Geodetska uprava Republike Slovenije, vrsta podatka in čas, na katerega se podatki nanašajo`, here `Register naslovov` and its reference date.

redistribute-model.because: GURS's terms put the source statement on every publication of `podatkov ali izdelkov`, data or products, so the weights are published with that statement in their rights files. If they are not Adapted Material, the licence does not reach them.

commercial-sublicense.because: §2(a)(1) grants a `non-sublicensable` licence, so this repository cannot sublicense the data. §2(a)(5)(A) offers every recipient a licence from GURS directly on the same source-statement condition.

The data is not guaranteed to be 100% accurate, correct, or complete. … Cook County or its staff assume no liability whatsoever for any losses that might occur from the use, misuse, or inability to use its geospatial data, maps or websites.` It grants no right to copy, adapt or redistribute. The MapServer service description, `https://gis.cookcountyil.gov/traditional/rest/services/addressZipCode/MapServer?f=pjson`, 3,492 bytes, sha256 `852534ffab53fd7f35c436f4b2b72737ec4ed8ba4c521aab293b97c797f3ec94`, states `copyrightText` `Cook County GIS` and nothing more; layer 0, 148,643 bytes, sha256 `0d72fcf2168c629644351717a8b342d889e3439a7ee785ac487797e1dce1ca58`, has an empty description and copyright. licenses.electedBecause: The District states two terms that apply in order, and the dataset's own notice governs. OpenAddresses' source record `sources/us/dc/statewide.json`, 2,406 bytes, sha256 `d63a225a797f764b79d15f5ba2bb740aec8d98a9d34301753a14b6aa64bad9ab`, downloads `https://opendata.dc.gov/api/download/v1/items/aa514416aaf74fdc94748f1e56e7cc8a/geojson?layers=0` and names `https://dc.gov/page/terms-and-conditions-use-district-data` as the licence. That page, 79,353 bytes, sha256 `fc7674c0a514cc3657e9df3284af8d464ced1d1c3e94fbc983de66e843f5063a`, reads: `Unless otherwise noted, the data on the Sites is public domain and made available with a Creative Commons CC0 1.0 Universal dedication. In short, the District waives all rights to the data worldwide under copyright law … You can copy, modify, distribute, and perform the data, even for commercial purposes, all without asking permission.` and `While not required, we ask that you give proper credit when using data from the Sites in your own work. … Data retrieved from Open Data DC catalog ( https://opendata.dc.gov )`. The item the download names, `aa514416aaf74fdc94748f1e56e7cc8a`, `Address Points`, owner `DCGISopendata`, `accessInformation` `Office of the Chief Technology Officer`, retained as `dc-item-aa514416.json`, 2,871 bytes, sha256 `e582e3ef45a15b0e6b3828207fae103061aec971428dd6c27c1320a9230824b6`, notes otherwise: its `licenseInfo` reads `This work is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License.` linking `https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0`. Because the item is `otherwise noted`, the election is CC BY 4.0, the more conditioned of the two; the operations it permits are a subset of what CC0 would permit, so the reading cannot overstate the grant. CC BY 4.0's legal code, `https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/legalcode.en`, 48,742 bytes, sha256 `58230517b7895aa219ff46a6ed63e67057a1582fb9ea054b16728a8c13525650`, §2(a)(1) grants `a worldwide, royalty-free, non-sublicensable, non-exclusive, irrevocable license … to: reproduce and Share the Licensed Material, in whole or in part; and produce, reproduce, and Share Adapted Material`. The credit is `Office of the Chief Technology Officer, District of Columbia, Address Points, Open Data DC (https://opendata.dc.gov), CC BY 4.0, changed`.

fetch.because: CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(A) grants the right to reproduce the material, which covers downloading the GeoJSON export.

extract.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material, which covers reading the address number, street, quadrant, city, state and ZIP columns.

transform.because: §2(a)(1)(B) grants adaptation for any purpose, so a token and tag corpus is permitted with the change indicated under §3(a)(1)(B).

train.because: §2(a)(1)(A) grants reproduction and §2(a)(1)(B) grants producing Adapted Material for any purpose, commercial use included, and fitting a model performs both.

redistribute-data.because: The Share grant covers redistribution in any medium, conditioned on the §3(a) attribution and on adding no restriction beyond the licence.

redistribute-model.because: If trained weights are Adapted Material, §2(a)(1)(B) grants sharing them for any purpose on the §3(a) attribution and change-statement conditions; if they are not, the licence does not reach them. Either way publishing the weights is permitted, with the credit and the statement of changes in the package's rights files.

commercial-sublicense.because: §2(a)(1) grants a `non-sublicensable` licence, so this repository cannot sublicense the material. §2(a)(5)(A) offers every recipient a licence from the Licensor directly, so a commercial recipient takes the District's data from the District on the same credit condition rather than from this repository.

licenses.refusedBecause: The address fields this source reads are the Broadband Serviceable Location Fabric, which the FCC distributes only under a limited end-user licence from its contractor CostQuest, and none of that licence's tiers covers commercial model training. The `fcc-bdc` adapter reads `address_primary`, `city`, `state`, `zip` and `zip_suffix` keyed by `location_id` from a SQLite database built outside this repository (`packages/corpus/lib/us/adapters/fcc-bdc/README.md`). The FCC's help article `How Entities Can Access the Location Fabric`, `https://help.bdc.fcc.gov/hc/en-us/articles/10419121200923-How-Entities-Can-Access-the-Location-Fabric`, read through the help centre's article API as `fcc-zendesk-entities.json`, 8,385 bytes, sha256 `c0657b80e8a4a01e18f24e97d1bd2855f043f33f5cb69a20090e9233ec9d357b` (the HTML page answered 403), states: `The FCC’s National Broadband Map allows users to download data reported by providers on the broadband serviceable locations (or BSLs) they serve and the type of service offered at each BSL. These downloadable data are available by Location ID … To obtain more information about the location beyond its Location ID, such its address, geographic coordinates, and building type, users will need to obtain access to the Fabric.` and `There are two Tier 4 Fabric License Agreements, the Standard Agreement and the Research License. … The Standard Agreement can only be used for the purpose of generating challenge and crowdsource data as part of the Broadband Data Collection . The Tier 4 Research License additionally supports non-commercial academic or public-policy research directly related to broadband availability.` The provider article (`fcc-zendesk-providers.json`, 7,937 bytes, sha256 `7854c01ad2319e7cf4dc085c639b225748e9609986fadb4d6b75fe63a9d4cdc8`) states `each service provider will need to execute a limited end-user license agreement`, scoped to `the counties in which they make broadband internet access service available`, and `Access to and use of the Fabric data will only be allowed via signing the published language in the agreement`; the government article (`fcc-zendesk-government.json`, 7,133 bytes, sha256 `fc85377060c8c380771637b237e6fbe3b5bbc749e62f79633079b62b31b5025a`) scopes government licences to `the counties in their jurisdiction`. So the public download carries no address, and every route to the address fields is a purpose-limited licence: BDC challenges, non-commercial broadband research, or a provider's or government's own service area. Training and publishing a commercially licensed general-purpose address parser is none of these. The adapter's README stamps rows `Public Domain` `per the FCC's federal-government distribution terms`; that holds for the FCC's own Location-ID-level availability files and not for the Fabric's addresses, so the stamp is wrong for every row this adapter emits. No tier the FCC describes reaches this use.

fetch.because: The address fields are obtained only by executing a CostQuest Fabric licence, and `Access to and use of the Fabric data will only be allowed via signing the published language in the agreement`.

extract.because: Each licence tier limits use to a purpose (BDC challenge data, non-commercial broadband research, or a licensee's own counties), and building a parser corpus is outside each.

transform.because: A derivative made for a purpose the licence does not name is outside it.

train.because: The Research License is limited to `non-commercial academic or public-policy research directly related to broadband availability`, and the Standard Agreement `can only be used for the purpose of generating challenge and crowdsource data`; commercial model training is neither.

redistribute-data.because: The licence is a limited end-user agreement naming licensee, administrator and recipients; publishing Fabric addresses to the public is outside it.

redistribute-model.because: Whether weights are a derivative does not arise where the underlying use is refused.

commercial-sublicense.because: The FCC states that CostQuest and the FCC `cannot entertain any changes to the language of the agreement`, and the agreement is a limited end-user licence with named recipients, so no right exists to sublicense.

The same section excepts material `contributed or licensed by private individuals, companies, or organizations`. The Public Libraries Survey outlet file is IMLS's own statistical compilation of what state library agencies report under its survey, published by IMLS at `https://www.imls.gov/sites/default/files/2025-08/pls_fy2023_csv.zip`, so it is the agency's work rather than third-party licensed material. The register row's `sourceURL`, `https://www.imls.gov/research-evaluation/data-collection/public-libraries-survey`, now answers HTTP 404; the fetcher's ZIP URL is the artifact this covers.

extract.because: Reading columns out of a work no copyright protects is unrestricted by copyright.

transform.because: Adaptation is an exclusive right only where copyright subsists, and section 105 denies it here.

licenses.electedTerms: OPEN-NY Terms of Use
licenses.electedBecause: The dataset `Commissioned NYS Notaries Public` (`rwbv-mz6z`), attributed to `New York State Department of State (DOS)`, carries no license field of its own in `https://data.ny.gov/api/views/rwbv-mz6z.json`, 31,799 bytes, sha256 `2adad1eae4e6226975d7c4de79422a96694c370912415bcd296b232b871919a4`, so the portal's terms govern. Those are the OPEN-NY Terms of Use, `https://data.ny.gov/download/77gx-ii52/application%2Fpdf`, served as `OPEN-NY Terms of Use.pdf`, 128,817 bytes, sha256 `9437c849705d58df008f01fc23f404444becce6b86676adc3974f9160a4cb650`, `LAST MODIFIED: March 8, 2013`, six pages read in full. The cover page states `use our government information however you wish, in private sector projects` and that the terms `do not contain restrictions requiring members of the public to use attribution, to re-post the license terms with any re-uses of the data, to impose share-alike or technical restrictions, nor require the public to obtain pre-approval before re-use of the data`, and `So long as you are not doing anything malicious with NYS data, you may use it as you wish, subject to no other requirements.` The operative clause under `Intellectual Property` is `The State grants you a non-exclusive, revocable license to use the Content contained on this website in a manner consistent with the Terms of Use`, and the adaptation verbs appear only as a limit on use `inconsistent with the Terms of Use`: `you will not reproduce, modify, adapt, prepare derivative works based on … OPEN-NY Content in a manner inconsistent with the Terms of Use`. Three conditions carry forward. The license is revocable: `Upon termination, all licenses and other rights granted to you in these Terms of Use will immediately cease`. `Any rights not expressly granted herein are reserved.` And use must be lawful, including compliance with intellectual property laws. The rows name individual notaries with business addresses; the terms state that content `has been vetted by the government agencies supplying the Content in order to reasonably ensure that information protected from disclosure by law is not released`, and impose no personal-data condition beyond lawful use, so that question belongs to this source's personal-data review, which `source-resolutions.json` does not yet hold.

fetch.because: `You are welcome to freely download and use this Content as long as you abide by these Terms of Use`.

extract.because: The license is `to use the Content`, and reading columns out of the export is use.

transform.because: The terms forbid modification and derivative works only `in a manner inconsistent with the Terms of Use`, and the cover page states the terms impose no share-alike and no pre-approval, so a lawful derived corpus is consistent with them.

train.because: `use our government information however you wish, in private sector projects`; fitting a model is a lawful private-sector use.

redistribute-data.because: The terms invite users to `share` the Content and state they impose no attribution or re-posting requirement, so republishing rows needs no credit line, though crediting the Department of State is courtesy.

redistribute-model.because: The cover page states the data may be used `as you wish, subject to no other requirements` than lawful use, with no share-alike, so weights fitted on it carry no condition from these terms.

commercial-sublicense.because: The grant is a `non-exclusive, revocable license` to the user, `Any rights not expressly granted herein are reserved`, and the terms state no sublicensing right; whether a downstream recipient holds the terms directly as a user of OPEN-NY, and how revocation would reach a sublicense, the text does not answer.

The OpenAddresses team does its best to summarize the source licenses in the source JSON for each source.` and `The source JSON in this repo (in the sources/ directory) is licensed under the CC0 1.0 Universal (CC0 1.0) Public Domain Dedication ... The rest of the repository is licensed under the BSD 3-Clause License`. The BSD licence, 1,480 bytes, sha256 `0166cd89016fcfb1e1b1ed736507a384865e875c5bb7ee7bd07545312f50a3ee`, and `sources/LICENSE`, 419 bytes, sha256 `9e90a0117df55c4dd3f1bace28c79a25da71832035f3d7304548d573cc627a22`, cover the code and the source definitions, not the addresses. licenses.electedTerms: Overture Maps per-theme terms: Places theme under CDLA Permissive 2.0 (Apache 2.0 for Foursquare records, CC0 1.0 for AllThePlaces records); Addresses theme under each source's own licence as Overture's attribution page lists it and each row's sources[].license names
licenses.electedBecause: This repository reads two Overture themes, and Overture licenses them differently. Neither is OpenStreetMap-derived: the places guide, `https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/places/`, 161,971 bytes, sha256 `37f2dd69d1971a1e23cd43c77bf7d51031a13c57dd9f21c7c5ca7e7ac9d168c5`, states `The theme is published under the CDLA Permissive 2.0 and Apache 2.0 licenses. It contains no OpenStreetMap data and carries none of the share-alike obligations of the Open Database License (ODbL)`, and the base, buildings, divisions and transportation themes, which carry ODbL, are not read. **Places** (`fragment-venue-bare`, `spliced-venue-locality`, and venue names and `poi.db` lexicon entries in `spliced-sub-venue`): the attribution page, `https://docs.overturemaps.org/attribution/`, 125,952 bytes, sha256 `505d216b53064565c917110999e215fb04cbdabdf85b9332ef84c367792c57b2`, lists Meta, Microsoft, PinMeTo, Krick, RenderSEO, DAC and BrightQuery under CDLA Permissive 2.0, Foursquare under Apache 2.0 (`Copyright 2024 Foursquare Labs, Inc. All rights reserved. Available under Apache 2.0`) and AllThePlaces under CC0 1.0. CDLA Permissive 2.0, `https://cdla.dev/permissive-2-0/`, 145,137 bytes, sha256 `fc9bdd715ca64b4e150348f07944698f7b8ebef2a507aae021afa7dc868c100e`, states `1.1. A Data Recipient may use, modify, and share the Data made available by Data Provider(s) under this agreement if that Data Recipient follows the terms of this agreement.`, `2.1. A Data Recipient may share Data, with or without modifications, so long as the Data Recipient makes available the text of this agreement with the shared Data.` and `3.1. This agreement does not impose any restriction or obligations with respect to the use, modification, or sharing of Results.`, with `5.4. "Results" means any outcome obtained by computational analysis of Data, including for example machine learning models and models' insights.` Apache 2.0, 11,358 bytes, sha256 `cfc7749b96f63bd31c3c42b5c471bf756814053e847c10f3eb003417bc523d30`, grants reproduction, derivative works and sublicensing with the licence and NOTICE kept. **Addresses** (`overture`, `overture-jp`, `overture-latam`, `overture-tw`, `rendered-sg-register`, the alignment indexes for `gcis-tw` and `houjin-jp`, and US skeletons in `invented-house-venue` and `spliced-sub-venue`): the addresses guide, `https://docs.overturemaps.org/guides/addresses/`, 61,781 bytes, sha256 `017231a5a5b29c2a5a487c584eccdc2c94e89bf7927ef2e57bc0f511366ca34e`, states `Because it aggregates many independent datasets, the theme carries a variety of source licenses rather than a single overall license.`, and the attribution page states `The addresses data comes from a variety of sources. All carry permissive open licenses. Some have special terms or require attribution.` For the countries the adapters read it lists Spain `scne.es` CC BY 4.0, Italy ANNCSU CC BY 4.0, the Netherlands BAG CC0 1.0, France the national address base under Licence Ouverte 2.0, Japan MLIT CC BY 4.0, Taiwan's county civil-affairs offices CC BY 4.0, Singapore Land Authority under the Singapore Open Data Licence, Canada Statistics Canada's Open Licence (with Yukon and Quebec under their own), Mexico INEGI under `TÉRMINOS DE LIBRE USO DE LA INFORMACIÓN DEL INEGI`, and the United States NAD plus county and state bodies. Overture grants no licence of its own over the addresses: the grant for each row is its source's, which Overture names on the row in `sources[].license`. Two gaps follow from Overture's own list. Portugal reads `Instituto Nacional de Estatística . Distributed by OpenAddresses` with no licence named, and three Michigan counties (Allegan, Kent, Muskegon) are `subject to a non-exclusive, limited, and revocable license` under county data agreements. This election does not reach an address row whose `sources[].license` names no licence or one of those county agreements. The `overture` adapter stamps every address row with `OVERTURE_DEFAULT_LICENSE = "CDLA-Permissive-2.0"` (`packages/corpus/lib/adapters/overture/adapter.ts`), which is the places licence, not the addresses theme's; the row-level licence needs to come from `sources[].license` for the exclusion above to be applied.

fetch.because: CDLA Permissive 2.0 §1.1 permits use of the places data. Overture distributes the addresses theme publicly under its sources' licences, each of which Overture states is a permissive open licence.

extract.because: CDLA Permissive 2.0 §1.1 permits modification, and Apache 2.0 §2 permits derivative works. For addresses, the named source licences (CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1), CC0, Licence Ouverte 2.0, the Statistics Canada and Singapore open licences) permit adaptation. The permission does not cover address rows whose source names no licence (Portugal INE) or a Michigan county data agreement.

transform.because: Same grants as extract: CDLA §1.1 modification for places, and each address source's adaptation grant. The same address-row exclusion applies.

train.because: CDLA Permissive 2.0 §3.1 places no restriction on Results, which §5.4 defines to include machine learning models. For addresses, the named open licences permit commercial use with attribution. The permission does not cover address rows whose source names no licence or a Michigan county data agreement.

redistribute-data.because: CDLA §2.1 permits sharing places data with the agreement's text included; Apache 2.0 records need the licence and Foursquare's NOTICE. Address rows may be shared with their source's attribution as Overture's attribution page states it, as the CC BY 4.0 sources' §3(a) requires. The same address-row exclusion applies.

redistribute-model.because: CDLA §3.1 imposes no obligation on Results, so weights trained on places data carry none. Address sources' attribution is carried in the model's rights files, as the CC BY 4.0 sources require.

commercial-sublicense.because: The address sources are mostly CC BY 4.0, whose §2(a)(1) grant is `non-sublicensable`, and each address source's grant runs to every recipient directly. CDLA Permissive 2.0 likewise reaches every Data Recipient, `directly or indirectly` (§5.3), so a commercial recipient takes the data from Overture's sources rather than from this repository. Weights trained on places data are Results under CDLA §3.1 and need no sublicence.

The two documents retrieved today are byte-identical to that decision's copies. The data repository's `LICENSE.md`, `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/whosonfirst/whosonfirst-data/master/LICENSE.md`, 725 bytes, sha256 `634276f100c598a3f8b79250a852383278857868a2d5efcf6639d485ae4a2cb0`, states: `Crediting Who's On First is recommended and linking back to the License is required. For example: > Data from Who's On First. [License](https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/).`, then `The Who's On First dataset is both an original work and a modification of existing open data. Some of those open data projects do require attribution.`, and puts `The format and structure that allows Who's On First to operate` under a Creative Commons Zero designation. The licences page, `https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/`, 48,404 bytes, sha256 `bb584e412810ef475b32264bf1d2b5c12f188006d5929b9441f56c2b5ddfc0ed`, repeats that text and lists 102 contributing sources, each with its own licence link. The links are open-data licences in the large majority (CC BY 2.0/2.5/3.0/4.0, CC0, OGL v2.0 and v3.0, the Canadian federal, provincial and municipal open government licences, DL-DE BY 2.0, Licence Ouverte, Swisstopo's free geodata conditions, the Census Bureau's terms, GeoNames under CC BY 4.0, Quattroshapes under CC BY 2.0, Natural Earth's public-domain terms). A few link a site-wide copyright page rather than a data licence: ISO's and ITU's copyright pages, which carry country and region codes, and Wikipedia's copyright page, whose text is CC BY-SA. The statement reserves nothing and names the link as its one required condition. It grants no licence of its own over Mapzen's original work beyond the format and structure, so this election reads the statement as permission conditioned on the link, together with the sources' own grants, and the credit set is the whole 102-source list because the admin database records a geometry source per record and no name source. What this repository reads under this row: place names, placetypes and parent ids from the WOF admin SQLite for locality, county and region tuples (`invented-house-venue-v063`, `invented-no-street`, `invented-no-street-v063`, `invented-po-box`), CN rows of the coarse-placer sample, locality spans in `fragment-assay`, seed rows of the `deepseek-translit-*` recipes, and US ZIP codes from `postalcode-us.db` in `invented-anchor-absorption`. A place name, a placetype, a parent relation and a ZIP code are facts each source also states; none of these reads copies a source's descriptive text.

extract.because: The statement describes the dataset as a modification of open data and reserves nothing. The contributing sources' licences grant adaptation, which covers reading place names, placetypes, parent ids and postal codes out of the databases.

transform.because: Joining a place to its parents and writing locality, county and region tuples adapts the records, which the contributing licences grant on their attribution conditions (for example CC BY 4.0 §2(a)(1)(B), OGL v3.0 `adapt the Information`).

License: https://whosonfirst.org/docs/licenses/` and the contributing sources' credits, which the licences page lists. CC BY-SA text from Wikipedia does not reach a row: the rows carry names and codes, not article text.

So this is the one OCDS election of the five that rests on the licensor rather than on the registry alone. The licence names no SPDX identifier, which is why none is recorded. The Authorization clause grants, `for commercial and non-commercial use`, that the data `may be: alienated, reproduced, distributed, published, translated, adapted, transformed, communicated or made available to the public through any form or procedure; merged with own and third-party data, and can be combined to form new and independent data sets; integrated into business processes, products and internal and external applications in public and private electronic networks`. The Note of Origin clause conditions all of it: `the name of the provider, the reference to the “Open Data License - Uruguay”. the reference to the data set that is being used`, and `Changes, editions, new designs or modifications must be mentioned in the note of origin`. The licensor's own page at catalogodatos.gub.uy answers HTTP 404, so the registry's quotation is the copy retained.

fetch.because: The Authorization clause grants that the data may be `reproduced`, which is what copying the published release performs.

extract.because: The clause grants that the data may be `adapted, transformed` and `combined to form new and independent data sets`, which covers reading the address fields out of it.

transform.because: The clause grants adaptation and transformation, and the Note of Origin requires that `Changes, editions, new designs or modifications must be mentioned`, so the obligation is a disclosure rather than a restriction.

train.because: The clause grants that the data may be `integrated into business processes, products and internal and external applications`, which is the act a model fitted on the rows performs.

redistribute-data.because: The clause grants that the data may be `distributed, published` and `made available to the public through any form or procedure`, conditioned on the Note of Origin naming the provider, the licence and the dataset.

redistribute-model.because: Integration into a product is granted, and whether releasing weights is that act or the redistribution of a derived data set is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records. licenses.electedTerms: Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0
licenses.electedBecause: SIRENE offers one licence and no alternative. data.gouv.fr's dataset page records `Producteur Institut national de la statistique et des études économiques (Insee)` and `Licence Licence Ouverte / Open Licence version 2.0`, and its API answers `license: lov2` for the same dataset. The licence text names SIRENE as its own worked example for attribution: `Dans le cas d'une réutilisation de la base SIRENE de l'INSEE, mentionner l'URL du « Concédant » : www.insee.fr + la date de dernière mise à jour de l'Information réutilisée.` The attribution owed is therefore the source and the date of the last update, and the mention must not suggest official endorsement. No share-alike term applies: the licence states it was designed to be compatible with any free licence requiring attribution at a minimum, naming OGL, CC-BY and ODC-BY. It settles no personal-data question, which it says in terms: personal data `peut être librement réutilisée` only `à condition de respecter le cadre légal relatif à la protection des données à caractère personnel`.

fetch.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants the reuser freedom `de la communiquer, la reproduire, la copier`, which is what copying the published stock file performs.

extract.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants freedom `de l'adapter, la modifier, l'extraire et la transformer, notamment pour créer des « Informations dérivées »`. Reading the address columns out of the stock file is the `extraire` in that clause.

transform.because: The same clause grants `la transformer, notamment pour créer des « Informations dérivées »`, and the licence defines an `Information dérivée` as any new data created directly from the Information. A token and tag corpus is such a work.

train.because: Fitting a model creates new information directly from the Information, which the licence's own definition of `Information dérivée` covers, and the grant for creating one is unconditional beyond attribution.

redistribute-data.because: Licence Ouverte 2.0 grants freedom `de la diffuser, la redistribuer, la publier et la transmettre, de l'exploiter à titre commercial, par exemple en la combinant avec d'autres informations, ou en l'incluant dans votre propre produit ou application`. Commercial reuse and inclusion in a product are named acts, subject to the attribution above.

redistribute-model.because: The licence grants creating an `Information dérivée` and grants redistributing `l'Information`, including by combining it with other information. Whether redistributing trained weights is one of those acts is the question `internal/strategy/counsel-briefing-2026-09-27-part-2.md` records, and this text does not state it. The grant here is wider than CC BY 3.0 AU's, so the answer may differ.

commercial-sublicense.because: The licence grants the reuser a non-exclusive right and states no term about granting that right onward. A recipient of redistributed Information is itself a `Réutilisateur` under the same licence, which is closer to needing no sublicence than to a sublicence being granted, and the text settles neither.

Clause 12(b) states that all contents in the system are the property of the KRPP. Clause 12(c) states `Asnjë përdorues nuk mund të kopjojë, modifikojë, publikojë, transmetojë, transferojë ose shesë, riprodhojë, krijojë vepra derivative, shpërndajë, shfaqë ose në ndonjë mënyrë të shfrytëzojë ndonjë nga përmbajtjet, tërësisht ose pjesërisht, me përjashtim i) kur ju lejohet me ligjet dhe rregulloret e prokurimit publik të Republikës së Kosovës, ose ii) me marrëveshjen e shprehur me shkrim të KRPP-së`: no user may copy, modify, publish, transmit, transfer, sell, reproduce, create derivative works from, distribute or display any of the contents, in whole or in part, except where the Republic of Kosovo's public procurement law permits it or by the express written agreement of the KRPP. Copying, extracting and fitting a model are each among the reserved acts. Two limits on this reading are recorded rather than resolved. The document governs the e-procurement portal and names the OCDS export nowhere, so whether the export is `contents in this system` is a reading rather than a statement; the export is a rendering of the portal's own records, which is why the refusal is taken as covering it. And clause 12(c)(ii) names a route to permission, so a written request to the KRPP could reverse this. The register's earlier record rested on the OCP Data Registry reading `License: -`, which is a third party's empty field rather than the publisher's statement, and this replaces it with the publisher's own words.

sources.name: NPPES
sources.authorityBasis: Regulatory/operational corpus retained from original Functionally Authoritative Address Corpora memo
sources.access: CSV bulk
sources.note: NPI registry; ~8M records; self-reported | mess=High

personalDataReview.because: NPPES Type 1 records name individual providers with their practice and mailing addresses, so the file carries records about identifiable natural persons. On 2026-10-29 the operator decided that the corpus keeps those rows as they are. The basis is HHS's FOIA determination in `HIPAA Administrative Simplification: National Plan and Provider Enumeration System Data Dissemination` (72 FR, document 07-2651, 2007-05-30): HHS reviewed the NPPES data elements under FOIA and the Privacy Act, withholds SSNs, IRS ITINs and dates of birth as `not disclosable under FOIA`, and publishes the remaining elements, the provider's name and addresses among them, in downloadable files. The rows carry only what HHS has determined to publish, and none of the withheld elements.

sources.name: Catastro INSPIRE Direcciones (AD)
sources.authorityBasis: Cadastral authority for Spain; publishes the INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme as an ATOM download service under its own access-and-use licence
sources.access: ATOM download service; one zipped GML per municipality
sources.note: The AD theme is an address point at a building entrance carrying a house-number designator; a thoroughfare name; a postcode and a municipality. It carries no party.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of the Dirección General del Catastro, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://www.catastro.hacienda.gob.es/INSPIRE/Addresses/ES.SDGC.AD.atom.xml`, 681,783 bytes, sha256 `4342d37b6d5527eb7b8bebadc97966c90f1a041068ae9398b90183f2176898b9`, carrying `<updated>2026-08-21T00:00:00Z</updated>`. The feed lists 55 entries, and this row covers 52 of them. The other three belong to the Provincial Councils of Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa and Navarra, which publish their own cadastres through the same feed and state their own terms, `CC BY 3.0 ES`, `CC-BY-SA` and `CC BY 4.0`. Adding them needs a row each, because a decision scoped to one publisher cannot reach another. Each of the 52 entries links a province feed listing one zipped GML per municipality. The measured instance is Ceuta, `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.zip`, 354,647 bytes, whose one member `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` is 11,861,975 bytes and holds 8,126 `AD:Address` features. A feature is a point at a building entrance carrying a house-number designator, and it references a thoroughfare name, a postal descriptor and an administrative unit by `xlink:href`. The row count for the other 51 offices was not measured.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `A.ES.SDGC.AD.55101.gml` was counted over all 11,861,975 bytes, so this covers the file rather than its first features. It holds 48 distinct element names and none of them names a party: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element, and no personal name of any kind. The only names are 505 `AD:ThoroughfareName`, 5 `AD:PostalDescriptor` and 1 `AD:AdminUnitName`. The file declares the INSPIRE Addresses 3.0 schema at `urn:x-inspire:specification:gmlas:Addresses:3.0`, which has no party element for another municipality to populate, so the reading rests on the schema as well as on the one municipality read. This is what separates the row from the other 25 `verified-corpus` sources: each of those is a business register or a procurement portal where the address belongs to a party, and some of those parties are natural persons trading on their own account. The cadastre's AD theme records the place. The ownership data that Spanish cadastral records also hold travels through a separate protected channel and appears nowhere in this dataset.

The measured instance is the first, `ES.BFA.AD.001.zip` for 48001 Abadiño, 108,613 bytes, whose one member `ES.BFA.AD.gml` is 5,902,666 bytes and holds 1,357 address features. The feature count for the other 111 municipalities was not measured. Bizkaia publishes this theme itself; Catastro's national feed links it rather than serving it, which is why it is a row of its own.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `ES.BFA.AD.gml` was counted over all 5,902,666 bytes, so this covers the file rather than its first features. It holds 49 distinct element names across 1,357 address features, and none of them is a party element: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element. **`AD:LocatorName` needs its values read rather than its name counted.** The INSPIRE Addresses guideline types it as a free-text `GeographicalName` and states that it `sometimes refer to the name of the family or business entity which at present or in the past has owned or occupied the property or building`, adding that it `must not be confused with the name of the addressee`. Bizkaia populates it on 1,357 of 1,357 features, and every value read is an internal cadastral reference rather than a name: they take the form `48 001 CL\TRAÑAETXOSTE(00066) 004`, which concatenates the municipality code 48001, a street-type abbreviation, the street name, its cadastral code and the house number. All 1,357 are distinct and each restates the address's own components. No value names a person.

sources.name: Gipuzkoa INSPIRE Addresses (AD)
sources.authorityBasis: Foral cadastral authority for Gipuzkoa; publishes its own INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme through an ATOM download service that Catastro's national feed links
sources.access: ATOM download service; one zipped GML for the whole province
sources.note: A feature is an address point with a house-number designator and a thoroughfare name. It carries no party.
sources.coverage: The INSPIRE Addresses (AD) theme of the Diputación Foral de Gipuzkoa, reached through the ATOM download service at `https://b5m.gipuzkoa.eus/inspire/download/addresses.xml`, 4,469 bytes, sha256 `27769a3cc85aacbc1bb5f9b1febc786f5433db8e6c6ad3892ba772adc58e9106`. The feed holds one entry covering the whole province rather than one per municipality, and it links its dataset through `rel="alternate"` rather than `rel="enclosure"`, so a reader that looks only for an enclosure finds no dataset here. That dataset, `https://b5m.gipuzkoa.eus/inspire/download/GML/ES.GFA.AD.zip`, is 7,959,103 bytes, and its one member `ES.GFA.AD.gml` is 313,162,472 bytes holding 68,744 address features. The feed states the refresh cadence as weekly and the reference system as EPSG:3042. This is the whole published extent rather than a sample of it.

personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `ES.GFA.AD.gml` was counted over all 313,162,472 bytes, so this covers the whole province rather than a sample of it. It holds 49 distinct element names across 68,744 address features, and none is a party element: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element. **This source needs the `AD:LocatorName` values read, and they are the case the standard warns about.** The INSPIRE Addresses guideline types that element as a free-text `GeographicalName` and states it `sometimes refer to the name of the family or business entity which at present or in the past has owned or occupied the property or building`, adding that it `must not be confused with the name of the addressee`. Gipuzkoa populates it on 46,365 of 68,744 features, giving 30,452 distinct values, and every value read is a building name published as a Basque and Spanish pair: `Gasolinera` with `Gasolindegia`, `Ayuntamiento` with `Udaletxea`, `Pabellón` with `Pabilioia`. Many are farmhouses, `Agirre, baserria` with `Agirre, caserío` and `Etxeberri, baserria` with `Etxeberri, caserío`, and a Basque baserri name is commonly also a surname. **The reading stays `absent` because these name the building rather than its occupant.** They are carried inside `GN:GeographicalName`, with the nativeness, name-status and language structure a toponym takes, and the guideline states that a locator name is not the addressee. A corpus built from this source therefore holds a place name whose etymology may be a family name, rather than a record about an identifiable person. Reading this field was the check the element census missed: that census treated `LocatorName` as place vocabulary without opening it.

The feed splits the province across 272 entries, each a zipped GML partition titled `Address Navarra` rather than named for a municipality, so a partition cannot be selected by place from the feed alone. personalDataReview.because: Every element name in `AD_Navarra_1.gml` was counted over all 307,117 bytes, so this covers that partition rather than its first features. It holds 29 distinct element names across 115 address features, and every one of the 29 belongs to the INSPIRE address, geographical-name or geometry vocabulary. No element identifies a party: there is no owner, holder, `titular`, occupant or contact element, and no personal name. The scope is one partition of 272; the reading extends to the rest through the INSPIRE Addresses schema, which has no party element for another partition to populate.

sources.coverage: ZPPA's OCDS release, Aug 2016 through May 2026 per the OCP Data Registry, 483,215 parties and 115,495 documents. Measured over the whole 2026 file, 13,244,085 bytes: 26,157 contracting processes and 62,736 party objects in four roles — tenderer 36,146, buyer 26,590, procuringEntity 26,590, supplier 5,014. A tenderer carries region, locality, countryName and streetAddress on 36,146 of 36,146 rows and a postcode on 29,982. Buyer and procuringEntity carry the same four on 26,590 of 26,590, and a sample shows one party holding both roles. A supplier carries region, locality and countryName on 5,014. The street field sometimes holds a post-office box — the Civil Aviation Authority reads `P.O.Box 50137` in `streetAddress` — so the field's grammar is mixed and a premise parser trained on it would see mailing forms.

personalDataReview.because: Two measures were run and neither establishes `absent`. No supplier or tenderer name among 36,146 counterparty party objects takes the `Surname, Firstname` form. Every one of those 36,146 carries an organization identifier under scheme `ZM-PCR`, and that settles nothing about the party's kind: PACRA registers sole-proprietor business names alongside companies, so both kinds of party carry the number. Of 9,500 distinct counterparty names, 853 carry no legal-form marker, and a sole trader trading under a shop name reads as a business by every shape test — `KAVULAMUNGU BARGAIN CENTRE` and `NDANJI SHOPPING CENTRE` among them. Every counterparty role here carries a street address on 100% of rows, so the exposure is whatever share of those 9,500 are individuals, which no measure available here bounds.
